name: Multimodal AI copilots
summary: Assistants combine text, speech, images and documents to help people understand information and complete work.
useCase: A field technician photographs an equipment panel, asks a spoken question and receives a cited maintenance explanation while keeping the final decision.
whyNow: Voice and image input reduce the effort needed to use AI, and assistants are increasingly distributed through devices and productivity software. OpenAI’s 2024 GPT-4o release is a useful technical milestone. Its 2026 disclosures place ChatGPT above 900 million weekly users, but that broad audience does not reveal how frequently people use voice, vision or work copilots.

mainstream.scope: Human-reviewed multimodal assistance in common office, learning and customer-support workflows among digitally connected users.
mainstream.rationale: Large existing assistant audiences and integration into familiar interfaces make this a near-term adoption wave. The definition requires routine useful assistance, not flawless factual performance. Sensitive, safety-critical or fully autonomous applications face a longer timetable, and sustained paid usage will matter more than launch-day interest.

metric.name: ChatGPT weekly active users — company proxy
metric.scope: OpenAI’s reported global ChatGPT audience across all modalities and purposes.
metric.limitations: Company-reported lower-bound snapshots, not audited modality-specific adoption. People using text only are included. The 2026 point is a dated observation, not a full-year average. No interpolation is provided for missing 2021–2023 measurements.
metric.futureNote: No comparable public forecast for weekly multimodal users is reliable enough to extrapolate. Track active modality use, retention and completed work instead.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No comparable multimodal-copilot user measurement identified.
No comparable modality-specific adoption series identified; text-chat use is not the same measure.
No like-for-like annual multimodal usage count is supplied.
GPT-4o introduced a unified text, vision and audio interface; ChatGPT exceeded 200 million weekly users.
OpenAI’s enterprise report described more than 800 million weekly ChatGPT users across use cases.
OpenAI reported over 900 million weekly users by May; this does not isolate multimodal activity.

tailwinds: Speech and cameras expand access beyond keyboard-based interactions.
Distribution through productivity suites and smartphones lowers discovery and onboarding costs.
bottlenecks: Confident factual errors and weak visual grounding require review.
Latency, accessibility, sensitive images and audio consent shape where the assistant is useful.
watchMetrics: Monthly retained users who use voice or vision, separated from total chatbot users.
Task completion, factual-error rates, latency and paid-seat retention in actual workflows.
